title: Heightmap-gradient particle filter on real DEM and 1 m LiDAR (SPRIN-D CTU method) vs TERCOM
summary: Re-implementation of the CTU SPRIN-D winner's localization (arXiv 2510.01348): local heightmap gradients matched to a prior DEM with the unnormalized correlation coefficient, Gaussian-blurred similarity maps weighting a translational particle filter resampled every fixed odometry distance, K-means largest-cluster estimate. Runs 10 km simulated flights with VIO-like drift over three real Copernicus GLO-30 windows (Bavarian Forest hills, Erding where SPRIN-D was flown, Hungarian plain) plus a smoothed-flat control, and compares against a radar-altimeter batch TERCOM baseline. Reports error vs distance, convergence from a 300 m initial offset, flat-terrain failure, a sensor-error sweep and measured CPU time per update. v2 adds a gain-fitted NCC likelihood with a Cramer-Rao information gate (falls back to odometry on featureless terrain: 336 vs 334 m at 10 km where v1 reached 539 m), compass bias as a particle state (8-53 m at 10 km for 0-20 deg bias where the translational filter loses lock above 10 deg), a no-truth confidence record (particle spread, ESS, CRB, NCC significance) checked against true error, and a test on real 1 m airborne LiDAR (Geobasis NRW DOM1/DGM1, dl-de/zero-2.0): the paper's literal binary edges reach 0.6 m median after 4 km at 1 m vs 19.9 m at 30 m reference resolution.
verified: ran 2026-11-06 with CPython 3.13.15 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 / rasterio 1.5.2 / matplotlib 3.11.2 on an Apple M2 Max: fetch_dem.py downloaded the three GLO-30 windows over public HTTPS, run_eval.py produced every number and plot in README (results deterministic across two full runs, timings vary with machine load), test_core.py 14 passed and fails when the correlation flip or similarity-map origin is mutated. The flights, odometry and heightmap sensor are simulated; no real UAV, LiDAR or SfM data was used. The paper's own numbers are quoted from the paper, not reproduced. v2 (same date and machine): test_v2.py 8 passed (22 total with test_core.py); run_eval_v2.py re-ran v1 pf_grad and matched out/results.json exactly in all four regions, then produced every v2 table and plot in README; fetch_lidar.py downloaded 32 Geobasis NRW 1 m tiles over public HTTPS; run_lidar.py produced the 1 m vs 30 m table and gave identical error numbers on two runs. v2 gate thresholds were tuned on seeds 100-111 of the same regions. The LiDAR test simulates the onboard map from the same NRW DSM plus noise.
shows: Heightmap-gradient particle filter and radar-altimeter TERCOM on real GLO-30 terrain; v2 information gate, compass-bias state, confidence, 1 m LiDAR
runtime: fetch ~25 s, v1 ~105 s, v2 ~6 min
key_result: [v2 at 10 km](README.md#1-information-gate-never-worse-than-odometry-on-flat-terrain): median 12 m hilly, 27 m mixed, 25 m flat vs odometry 311-404 m (20 runs)
